question: A certain sum on simple interest becomes ₹49,600 in 3 years and ₹56,000 in 5 years. If the rate of interest had been 2% more, then in how many years would the sum have doubled?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/661340121ece4245dffae37dda41ddab0ce1f2bf0ba4a0210bff82185deedb2e.png] __Shortcut Trick__

On simple interest, a certain sum becomes Rs. ₹49,600 in 3 years and ₹56,000 in 5 years.

The total interest in 2 years = 56000 - 49600 = Rs. 6400

The total interest in 1 year = 6400/2 = Rs. 3200

The total interest in 5 years = 3200 × 5 = Rs. 16000

So, the total amount = 56000 - 16000 = Rs. 40000

The rate of percentage = (3200/40000) × 100 = 8%

The new rate of percentage = 8 + 2 = 10%

So, time required 100%/10% = 10 years
